description: Built November 1944 by Douglas at Long Beach California; flown as a Living History Flight aircraft and hangared at Mesa for walk-through tours between tour legs; titled to the American Airpower Heritage Flying Museum of Dallas Texas which is normal for CAF aircraft

Flew 15 combat missions with the 319th Bomb Group 437th Bomb Squadron from Serragia Corsica between 4 November and 31 December 1944 as Battle Number 18; tours nationally each summer and is hangared at Mesa between tours
aliases: 43-35972; TB-25N; Battle Number 18; B25; B25J; TB25N

description: Served with the 11th Troop Carrier Squadron on clandestine supply and agent-insertion flights from Brindisi Italy into the Balkans in 1944; later a corporate aircraft then owned by the Wings of Flight Foundation; the FAA gives construction number 9380 and year of manufacture 1943 but no wartime USAAF serial could be corroborated so none is recorded
aliases: c/n 9380; DC-3; Dakota; C47; C47A; DC3

description: Flown for passenger rides and hangared at the museum; the FAA registration N145AZ records it as a Beech D18S construction number A-235; the serial 44511 printed by two directories is unverified and looks like a construction number in a serial field
aliases: N145AZ; D18S; Beech 18; c/n A-235; C45

description: The FAA gives construction number 75-7540 and year of manufacture 1943; flown for passenger rides from the museum
aliases: PT-17; Stearman; Model 75; B75N1; c/n 75-7540; PT17

description: Bureau Number 90725 per the FAA construction-number field; flown for passenger rides at the museum; the FAA year-of-manufacture field reads 1959 which cannot be right for an SNJ-5 so no year is recorded

Listed in the museum's flying fleet on a page titled L-19E but no registration is published; two Cessna 305C O-1E airframes are registered to the CAF and it could not be established which is the Mesa aircraft so the tail number is left blank
aliases: L-19; Bird Dog; O1; O1E; L19

description: Listed on the museum's own 2026 collection page; the surviving-Invader list also places it at CAF Mesa; however the FAA now shows registration N202R held by Lone Star Express LLP of Grand Junction Colorado so continued presence at Mesa needs confirming

Bureau Number 126731; the FAA registry names the owner as Commemorative Air Force which is good live evidence of continued CAF ownership; the FAA year-of-manufacture field reads 1940 which is impossible for an AF-2S so no year is recorded

Listed on the museum's own 2026 collection page; photographed at Mesa in June 2012 carrying the number 4048 which one directory repeats while another gives 4115; neither is tied to a construction number so no identity is recorded; many US-displayed MiG-15bis airframes are Polish Lim-2 or Chinese J-2 licence builds and this one is unresolved

Listed on the museum's own 2026 collection page as a Sikorsky H-19 S-55 Chickasaw; the serial 54-1416 and registration N6735 that circulate in directories do not check out because N6735 is not on the current FAA register and 54-1416 does not sit in a USAF H-19 production block so no identity is recorded
Training glider suspended from the hangar roof; the serial 18 quoted by one directory is unverified so no identity is recorded
Listed on the museum's own 2026 collection page; the registration N7436B quoted by directories is now a Champion 7EC owned by a private individual in Las Vegas Nevada so it is not recorded here
Target drone suspended from the hangar roof; the museum's own collection page credits it as Radioplane Frankfort; no serial published

Homebuilt reproduction of the WWI Nieuport 17 built by Michael P Wray with FAA serial 251; this is a reproduction and not an original; the museum's own 2026 collection page still lists it but the FAA transferred N124RX to a private owner in Omaha Nebraska in October 2023 so continued presence needs confirming
Full-size replica of the Nieuport 28 flown by Eddie Rickenbacker; explicitly a replica and not an original; the museum publishes no builder or identity
Replica triplane listed on the museum's own 2026 collection page; no builder identity or registration published so it is recorded as a replica of unknown build
Replica of the Fokker E.V D.VIII parasol monoplane; the registrations NX7757U and NX7557U quoted by two directories match nothing on the current FAA register so no identity is recorded
Suspended from the hangar roof; almost certainly a replica although the museum does not say so; one directory quotes 26238 which is unverified

Suspended from the hangar roof at Mesa; the museum publishes no identity and does not say whether it is original or a replica; a separate genuine SPAD XIII hangs in Terminal 3 at Phoenix Sky Harbor and the two should not be confused
